questions.question: In digital integrated circuit design and Design for Testability (DFT), what is the primary operational objective of inserting scan chains by replacing conventional flip-flops with scan flip-flops?
options: To improve combinational logic delay and maximize the functional operating frequency (f_max) of the design.
To transform sequential circuit testing into combinational circuit testing by providing direct controllability and observability of internal state elements.
To automatically correct soft errors caused by cosmic rays and alpha particles during runtime execution.
To eliminate clock skew across long-distance distribution networks without requiring balanced clock trees.
To dynamically compress automated test pattern generation (ATPG) vectors directly inside the logic gates.

questions.question: In modern pipelined microprocessor front-ends, what is the fundamental functional distinction between a Branch Target Buffer (BTB) and a directional branch predictor (such as a 2-bit saturating counter array)?
options: A BTB tracks loop iteration trip counts, whereas a directional predictor tracks return addresses for nested subroutine calls.
A BTB predicts whether an indirect branch will trigger an architectural exception, whereas a directional predictor checks memory permissions.
A BTB is implemented in software within the operating system kernel, whereas a directional predictor is purely a microarchitectural hardware structure.

A BTB provides the predicted target memory address of an instruction during the fetch stage before instruction decoding, whereas a directional predictor determines whether a conditional branch is taken or not taken.
A BTB resolves data hazards caused by branch conditions, whereas a directional predictor resolves structural hazards in the arithmetic logic units.

questions.question: In low-power synchronous digital design, why is an Integrated Clock Gating (ICG) cell structured with an active-low level-sensitive latch before the gating AND gate, rather than simply using a standalone two-input AND gate to gate the clock signal?
options: It prevents hazards and runt pulses (glitches) on the gated clock output by ensuring the enable signal can only change state while the master clock is low.
It shifts the phase of the gated clock by 180 degrees to eliminate setup time violations in the downstream flip-flops.
It doubles the output drive strength of the clock net to avoid the necessity of inserting intermediate clock buffer trees.
It reduces the static leakage current of the downstream register bank to zero when the clock is held high.
It allows the clock gate to function as a dynamic level shifter between disparate supply voltage domains.

questions.question: In deep-submicron Static Timing Analysis (STA) and signal integrity analysis, how does capacitive crosstalk coupling affect net delay when an 'aggressor' net and a parallel 'victim' net switch simultaneously in opposite directions?
options: The effective coupling capacitance is virtually eliminated due to electrostatic shielding, minimizing wire delay.
The mutual inductance dominates, inducing an opposite polarity ringing pulse that speeds up victim signal propagation.
The effective coupling capacitance between the nets is amplified due to the Miller effect, significantly increasing the victim net's transition time and propagation delay.
The victim net's signal transition is accelerated toward the opposite supply rail, potentially resulting in a hold time violation.
The ground bounce on the common substrate neutralizes the crosstalk voltage spike, leaving timing completely unaffected.

questions.question: In modern multi-core computer memory controllers, what is the primary scheduling principle of the First-Ready First-Come-First-Served (FR-FCFS) DRAM arbitration policy?
options: It strictly prioritizes memory requests originating from high-priority CPU cores over background DMA write bursts regardless of row status.
It always alternates between read and write requests on every clock cycle to prevent the command bus from floating.
It services requests in strict chronological arrival order, only breaking ties using DRAM bank availability.
It schedules write operations only when the controller queues are completely full, executing a forced write-drain epoch.
It prioritizes requests that access already activated (open) DRAM row buffers before older requests targeting closed or conflicted rows, thereby maximizing row-buffer locality and bus throughput.
